'''Jared Sullinger''' (born March 4, 1992) is an [[United States|American]] college [[basketball]] player. As a sophomore at [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], Sullinger announced at a press conference on April 4, 2012 that he will be leaving school to enter the [[2012 NBA Draft]]. <ref>http://www.buckeyextra.com/content/stories/2012/04/04/0404-ohio-state-sullinger-news-conference.html</ref>

==High school career==
He was rated as the number 2 player in the class of 2010 in the [[ESPNU]] 100<ref>{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2010&action=upsell&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2010 |title=College Basketball Recruiting - ESPNU 100 - ESPN |publisher=Insider.espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref> the number 4 player by [[Scout.com]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2010 |title=Scout.com: Football Recruiting |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref> and the number 5 player by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name=rivals>{{cite web|url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1909 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking - Rivals150 for class of 2010 |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref> In his senior year, Sullinger led Northland High School to a 21-0 season and a #1 national ranking. He averaged 24.5 points and 11.7 rebounds for the season.<ref name="dispatch1">{{cite web|url=http://www.dispatch.com/live/content/sports/stories/2010/03/10/naismith-awards.html |title=Northland High School basketball player, father win national Naismith awards |publisher=The Columbus Dispatch |date=2010-03-10 |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref> Sullinger played in the 4th annual [[Boost Mobile]] Elite 24 Hoops Classic.<ref>{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2009/08/boost-mobile-elite-24-roster-announced/ |title=Boost Mobile Elite 24 Roster Announced |publisher=Slam Online |date=2009-08-05 |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref>

Sullinger was selected to play in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American Game]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]],<ref>{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/02/mcdonalds-all-american-game-team-announced/ |title=McDonald’s All-American Game Team Announced |publisher=Slam Online |date=2010-02-11 |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref> where he was named co-MVP with [[Harrison Barnes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/m2xSkj0QEd-lugAcxJTdpg/mcdonalds-all-american-night--knights-3-pointer-wins-it-for-the-west.htm |title=McDonald's All-American night: Knight's 3-pointer wins it for the West - MaxPreps News |publisher=Maxpreps.com |date=2010-03-31 |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref> He was also selected to play in the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon]]<ref>{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/01/its-the-usa-against-everyone-else/ |title=It’s the USA Against Everyone Else |publisher=Slam Online |date=2010-01-20 |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref> and the 2010 [[Jordan Brand]] Classic at [[Madison Square Garden]] in [[New York]].<ref>{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/02/jordan-brand-all-american-game-team-announced/ |title=Jordan Brand All-American Game Team Announced |publisher=Slam Online |date=2010-02-18 |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref>

On March 10, 2010, Sullinger won the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|James A. Naismith Award]], which goes to the boys basketball player of the year.<ref name="dispatch1"/>

Sullinger committed to Ohio State on May 10, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.escoutroom.com/eScoutRoom/Articles/ArticlesDetail/tabid/702/smid/1331/ArticleID/898/Default.aspx |title=A Summer Full of Events for #1 Center in the Country, Jared Sullinger |publisher=Escoutroom.com |date=2007-05-05 |accessdate=2010-08-26}}</ref>

==College career==

====Freshman====
Sullinger had 19 points and 14 rebounds in his Ohio State debut.<ref>[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303160194 Ohio State routs North Carolina A&T in season opener]</ref>
Sullinger's brother, J.J. Sullinger also attended Ohio State and played for coach [[Thad Matta]]. For the 2010-2011 season Jared Sullinger averaged 17.2 points, 10.2 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in 31.7 minutes per game for the Buckeyes. Ohio State finished the regular season at 32-2 and was selected as the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA tournament's]] number one overall seed. The Buckeyes made it to the 'Sweet Sixteen' where they lost to [[Kentucky basketball|Kentucky]] 62-60. Sullinger was picked to the First Team All-America by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711|title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams|work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]]|publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|date=Mar 7, 2011|accessdate=June 21, 2011}}</ref>

====Sophomore====
In what would be his final year at Ohio State, Sullinger led the Buckeyes to a 31-8 overall record (13-5 Big Ten). Sullinger averaged 17.5 points and 9.3 rebounds per game during the 2011-12 season. The Buckeyes advanced to the 'Final Four' of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]], where the team lost to the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. Sullinger had 13 points in the game and was 5-of-19 shooting with 11 rebounds in the loss. Five days after the loss, the two-time AP All-American declared he was entering the 2012 draft, where he was widely expected to be a lottery pick, until he was reportedly flagged by several teams after the Chicago pre-draft camp due to back issues. He is now believed to go late 1st Round/early 2nd round.  <ref>http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/8069495/2012-nba-draft-docs-medically-red-flag-jared-sullinger-sources-say</ref>
